title: Setting a LARGE (oversize) tool
body:
## Know first
The magazine is random-pot. After M06 the spindle tool swaps with the next tool right away, so a tool does **not** go back to the pot it came from. The pot is the fixed thing, not the tool.

A tool sitting in the spindle cannot be edited — its TOOL SET value is locked. Get it back into a magazine pot first.

**LARGE** is not in the TOOL SET list at first. The control derives it from the pot layout once the neighbors are blocked out.

## Procedure
1. Run a tool change so the tool returns to the magazine.
2. Read the pot number off the POT DETAIL panel. Do not assume it is the pot it started in.
3. Pull any tools out of the pots on either side.
4. Each neighbor pot: **[EDIT]** soft key, cursor on TOOL SET, set to **INHI.**
5. Go back to the middle pot — **LARGE** shows up on its own.

## Verified
Cycled tool changes about 10 minutes and the tool held its pot. INHI takes both neighbors out of the swap pool, so the large tool has nowhere else to land.

## Watch out
- HEAVY and LARGE are different. HEAVY is weight and slows the ATC arm. LARGE is diameter.
- Confirm neighbor pot numbers against the magazine or the graphical view. List order is not always physical order.
- TOOL SET options on this control: NORMAL, HEAVY, LARGE, INHI., PROBE, CALIB.
- Probe is tool #60 on this machine.
- Max tool diameter is commonly listed as 80 mm, or 150 mm with empty adjacent pockets. Check the machine's own spec before trusting that.

title: Alarm "Sub Arm not in spindle side"
body:
## When it shows up
Mostly after **air pressure drops**, or an **E-stop during a tool change**.

## Fix
1. Move the spindle back to tool change position first: **G30 X0. Y0.** DO NOT skip this.
2. **Reset**
3. **Setting** ->; **Custom**->; **ATC**->; **MDI**
4. **#2 open ATC door**
5. **Pot unlock**
6. **Pot Spindle side**
7. **Pot Down**
8. **Pot Lock**
9. Hit **Program**, type **M6**, then **Cycle Start**.

title: Spline in MCAM
body:
Do **not** use a spline to chain a toolpath.

Project 3D toolpaths take forever to regenerate off a spline.

Draw a **line or arc** instead and chain to that.

title: G131 / HON — speed vs precision
body:
## What it does
One line in the program tells the machine how hard to trade **speed** against **precision**. Put it near the top, before the cutting.

## Touch panel machines — pick by job type
Low number = faster. High number = tighter. Middle = balanced, leaning tight.

- **G131P1-3** — prismatic. 2-axis and helical work.
- **G131M1-3** — multi-surface. 3-axis work.
- **G131F1-3** — 5-axis simultaneous. Works for 4-axis too.
- **G131D1** — drilling and tapping. Lets the machine accelerate harder, since canned cycles are positional and have no profile to hold.

For P, M and F: **1** = speed and smoothness, **3** = precision, **2** = a decent balance still leaning toward precision.

## Older R-level way
**HONR0-10** or **G131R0-10**. **0** = speed, **10** = precision, in between is a blend.

## Watch out
- HON still works, but it needs the right variable and value or it does nothing.
- A program containing HON has to be **loaded in** from USB, Compact Flash or RS-232. Typing it at the control will not work.
- Pick by what the job needs: roughing and drilling want speed, finish surfaces want precision.

## Source
Selway Machine Tool applications bulletin, 2/23/2021 — "Matsuura G131/HON Explained, New Matsuura Machines".
